records.label: spacr.power_simulate#3
records.source: A pooled Toxoplasma CRISPR screen has three noisy layers stacked on top of each other — which genotypes landed in which well, how many of a well's cells the microscope saw and how well the classifier called them, and how many reads each genotype got out of the amplicon pool. The question a screener has to answer *before* spending the microscope time is "with this library, this many wells, this many cells per well and a classifier at 0.80/0.12, would I actually find a hit?". That is a power analysis, and it is only answerable by simulation because no layer is analytically tractable once the other two are stacked on it.
records.context: A pooled Toxoplasma CRISPR screening experiment has three noisy layers stacked on top of each other — which genotypes landed in which well, how many of a well's cells the microscope saw and how well the machine-learning classification model called them, and how many reads each genotype got out of the amplicon pool. The question a screener has to answer *before* spending the microscope time is "with this library, this many microplate sample positions, this many cells per well and a machine-learning classification model at 0.80/0.12, would I actually find a hit?". That is a statistical detection sensitivity analysis, and it is only answerable by simulation because no layer is analytically tractable once the other two are stacked on it.
records.translation: साझा Toxoplasma CRISPR screening experiment में शोर की तीन परतें एक-दूसरे पर चढ़ी हैं—कौन-से genotype किस microplate sample position में पहुँचे, microscope ने किसी well के कितने cells देखे और ML वर्गीकरण मॉडल ने उन्हें कितनी अच्छी तरह पहचाना, तथा amplicon pool से हर genotype को कितने reads मिले। microscope समय खर्च करने से *पहले* screener को यह पूछना है: "इस library, इतने microplate sample positions, प्रति well इतने cells और 0.80/0.12 वाले ML वर्गीकरण मॉडल के साथ क्या मुझे वास्तव में कोई hit मिलेगा?"। यह सांख्यिकीय पहचान-संवेदनशीलता विश्लेषण है और इसका उत्तर simulation से ही मिल सकता है, क्योंकि बाकी दो परतें जोड़ने के बाद कोई भी परत analytically tractable नहीं रहती।

records.label: spacr.qt.ai.worker.make_stream_thread#4
records.source: ``worker.finished -> thread.quit`` is a **DirectConnection**. The QThread object is created here, on the GUI thread, so it is GUI-affine — a queued ``quit()`` is posted to the *GUI* thread's event queue, not to the worker's. Measured: with a queued connection, a GUI thread that goes straight into ``thread.wait()`` (which is exactly what ``ConsolePanel.shutdown`` and every "drain before closing" path does) waits out its whole timeout on a worker that has already finished, because the event that would stop the thread is sitting behind the wait. ``QThread::quit`` is explicitly thread-safe, so calling it inline from the worker thread is correct.
records.context: ``worker.finished -> thread.quit`` uses a **DirectConnection**. The QThread object is created on the GUI thread. That gives it GUI thread affinity. A queued ``quit()`` goes to the *GUI* event queue rather than the worker queue. The GUI thread immediately enters ``thread.wait()`` during the "drain before closing" behavior in ``ConsolePanel.shutdown``. This blocks the event that would stop the worker and waits for the full timeout even though the worker has finished. ``QThread::quit`` is thread-safe, so the worker thread may call it directly.
records.translation: ``worker.finished -> thread.quit`` एक **DirectConnection** उपयोग करता है। QThread object GUI thread पर बनता है, इसलिए उसकी affinity GUI thread से होती है। queued ``quit()`` worker queue के बजाय *GUI* event की queue में जाता है। GUI thread ``thread.wait()`` में प्रवेश करता है, जैसा ``ConsolePanel.shutdown`` के "drain before closing" व्यवहार में होता है। इससे worker रोकने वाला event block हो जाता है और worker पूरा हो जाने पर भी पूरा timeout लगता है। ``QThread::quit`` thread-safe है, इसलिए worker thread उसे सीधे बुला सकता है।

records.label: spacr.qt.job_runner#4
records.source: ``QThread.finished`` must be connected to a **bound method of a GUI-thread QObject**, never a closure. PySide6 makes the QThread itself the receiver for a closure, and :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread` connects ``thread.finished -> thread.deleteLater`` first. Slots run in connection order, so the DeferredDelete is posted ahead of the closure's metacall and Qt discards queued events for a destroyed receiver: the job is never retired and ``active_jobs()`` never returns to zero.
records.context: **QObject receiver requirement.** Connect ``QThread.finished`` to a method on a QObject that belongs to the GUI thread. A closure is unsafe. PySide6 assigns the QThread itself as a closure's receiver. :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread` first connects ``thread.finished -> thread.deleteLater``. Slots execute in connection order. DeferredDelete is therefore posted before the closure callback. Qt discards the queued callback after destroying its receiver. The job then remains active and ``active_jobs()`` never reaches zero.
records.translation: **QObject receiver की आवश्यकता।** ``QThread.finished`` को GUI thread से संबंधित QObject की method से जोड़ें; closure सुरक्षित नहीं है। PySide6 QThread को ही closure का receiver बना देता है। :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread` पहले ``thread.finished -> thread.deleteLater`` जोड़ता है। Slots connection order में चलते हैं, इसलिए DeferredDelete closure callback से पहले post होता है। receiver नष्ट होने के बाद Qt queued callback छोड़ देता है। तब job active रहती है और ``active_jobs()`` कभी zero तक नहीं पहुँचता।

records.label: spacr.qt.prerun#6
records.source: The banner **reads** a verdict; it does not compute one.  Opening a plate's masks costs seconds to minutes, and a screen that pays that on every visit is a screen nobody keeps.  So :func:`spacr.seg_qc.read_digest` parses the CSVs the mask run already wrote, dates each one against its mask stack, and reports a card older than its masks as OUT OF DATE rather than believing it.  Only the *Score the masks now* button scores anything, only when pressed, and it does it on a worker thread and writes the card so the next open is cheap again.
records.context: The banner **reads** a verdict; it does not compute one.  Opening a plate's masks costs seconds to minutes, and an application view that pays that on every visit is an application view nobody keeps.  So :func:`spacr.seg_qc.read_digest` parses the CSVs the mask run already wrote, dates each one against its mask stack, and reports a card older than its masks as OUT OF DATE rather than believing it.  Only the *Score the masks now* button scores anything, only when pressed, and it does it on a background execution unit and writes the card so the next open is cheap again.

records.label: spacr.qt.screens.db_browser#14
records.source: 1. :func:`spacr.qt.preferences.get_db_browser_editable` must be on — it is off by default and lives in Preferences, not on this screen. 2. The database must have been chosen explicitly in this session (``set_database(..., explicit=True)``). 3. The user must tick "Edit mode" *and* confirm; ticking alone does nothing. 4. The row must be addressable by ``rowid`` or a primary key. Without one, the edit is refused — an UPDATE matching on column values can hit many rows, which on a measurements table is silent mass corruption. The write also probes ``COUNT(*)`` for the row address first and rolls back unless ``rowcount == 1``. 5. The typed text must be coercible to the column's declared type. SQLite will cheerfully store ``'abc'`` in an INTEGER column; :func:`coerce_for_column` refuses instead.
records.context: Editing is allowed only when all five checks pass. 1. :func:`spacr.qt.preferences.get_db_browser_editable` is enabled in Preferences; it is off by default and is not on this screen. 2. This session explicitly selected the database with ``set_database(..., explicit=True)``. 3. The user selected "Edit mode" *and* confirmed it; selection alone does nothing. 4. The row has ``rowid`` or a primary-key identifier. Otherwise refuse the edit: matching column values could silently update many measurement rows. Before writing, probe ``COUNT(*)`` and roll back unless ``rowcount == 1``. 5. The text converts to the declared column type. SQLite accepts ``'abc'`` in an INTEGER column, but :func:`coerce_for_column` must refuse it.
records.translation: Editing केवल सभी पाँच checks के सफल होने पर अनुमत है। 1. :func:`spacr.qt.preferences.get_db_browser_editable` Preferences में enabled हो; यह डिफ़ॉल्ट रूप से off है और इस screen पर नहीं है। 2. इस session ने ``set_database(..., explicit=True)`` से database को स्पष्ट रूप से चुना हो। 3. उपयोगकर्ता ने "Edit mode" चुना *और* पुष्टि की हो; केवल चुनने से कुछ नहीं होता। 4. row में ``rowid`` या primary-key identifier हो। अन्यथा edit अस्वीकार करें: column values से match करने वाला UPDATE अनेक measurement rows को चुपचाप बदल सकता है। लिखने से पहले ``COUNT(*)`` जाँचें और ``rowcount == 1`` न होने पर rollback करें। 5. text को घोषित column type में बदला जा सके। SQLite INTEGER column में ``'abc'`` स्वीकार कर लेता है, लेकिन :func:`coerce_for_column` को इसे अस्वीकार करना चाहिए।
